In [[geometry]], the '''elongated pyramids''' are an infinite set of [[polyhedra]], constructed by adjoining an {{nowrap|{{mvar|n}}-gonal}} [[Pyramid (geometry)|pyramid]] to an {{nowrap|{{mvar|n}}-gonal}} [[Prism (geometry)|prism]]. Along with the set of pyramids, these figures are topologically [[Self-dual polyhedron|self-dual]].

There are three ''elongated pyramids'' that are [[Johnson solid]]s: 
* [[Elongated triangular pyramid]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|7}}}}),
*[[Elongated square pyramid]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|8}}}}), and
*[[Elongated pentagonal pyramid]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|9}}}}). 
Higher forms can be constructed with [[isosceles triangle]]s.
